images.caption: Front and southern side of the Henry Graefe House, located at 1429 Columbus Avenue in Sandusky, Ohio, United States.  Built in 1900 according to a William Warren Sabin design, it is listed on the Nati

brief: An island-town cottage lot: Henry Graefe House, a 19th-century Lake Erie house; see the photo for its massing, porch and trim. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: the Lake Erie shore towns that stand in for Victory Bay's island streets (Vermilion, Sandusky, Put-in-Bay) were built 1840-1920, and Commons has almost no newer cottages there. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Henry Graefe House (Sandusky OH, c.1900 remodel): a white Classical Revival house with a two-storey Corinthian portico and pediment with a lunette, a balcony, bay windows, a roof balustrade, a tall exterior chimney; a clipped hedge of boxwood along the front and a balustraded terrace

why.note: the 1893 Chicago fair's classicism, applied to a lake-port merchant's house
